findings.evidence: Fig 6.2 in-figure label (PDF p.143): 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)'. Its own caption: '...the p95 SLO is met (p95 ≈ 0.99 s ≤ 2 s), while 1% of requests exceed the 2 s request-latency line — the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget'. Book convention (Ch 4, PDF p.106): 'The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to'.
findings.issue: Figure-vs-caption/terminology defect: the plotted 2 s line is labelled 'TTFT budget' inside the figure, but the book's convention (Ch 4; Preface reading conventions) reserves 'budget' for the 1.2 s design budget and calls 2 s the 'p95 ceiling'. The caption explicitly makes this correction, so the in-figure label contradicts both its own caption and the cross-chapter terminology discipline (a load-bearing contrast per the Preface: 'load-bearing contrasts are never relaxed').
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the figure's 2 s line to 'SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)' (or 'p95 ceiling ≤ 2 s') so the in-figure label matches the caption and the Ch 4 budget-vs-ceiling distinction; sweep other figures plotting SLO lines (Ch 14/15 region) for the same wording.
